about: A second set of real UK and European families from open-access published case reports (collected 18 Oct 2026, weighted towards BRCA1/2, Lynch and TP53), each with a germline variant the authors report as causal (weaker evidence noted in 'notes'), transcribed by AI research agents from the full text and pedigree figures, with quotes in 'evidence' and judgement calls in 'notes'. Citations checked against PubMed on 18 Oct 2026. Kept separate so each set keeps its own floor; do not tune scoring to individual cases without a source.

cases.variant: c.4475_4476insAluYb8 in exon 14 (NM_007294.4); causes exon 14 skipping, r.4358_4484del p.(Ala1453Glyfs*10); authors consider it deleterious
cases.citation: Bouras A et al. Genes (Basel) 2021;12:1736
cases.evidence: 'Proband III-1 (Figure 1) developed a left breast cancer at age 42 years and a high-grade serous ovarian cancer at 47 ... The second proband II-2 developed an ovarian cancer at 72 ... a third subject (II-4) developed a left triple negative breast cancer at the age of 81.' 'The c.4475_4476insAluYb8 mutation was detected in the DNA samples from III-1 and II-2 but not from the unaffected siblings (II-5 and II-6).' RNA: 'total skipping of exon 14 ... frameshift and a premature stop codon ... deleterious variant'. Fig 1 pedigree: III-1 (B 1966, D 2018) '(42) BC RH+/HER2+, (47) OV', carrier; her mother II-2 (B 1944, D 2018) '(72) OV', carrier; her father II-1 (B 1942, D 2016) '(70) melanoma'; maternal aunt II-4 (B 1937) '(81) BC RH-/HER2-', carrier; maternal aunts II-5, II-7 'no cancer', non-carriers; maternal grandmother I-2 (B 1911, D 1967) '(56) unknown Cancer'.
cases.notes: The paper calls three family members 'probands'; III-1 (the first described, youngest generation) was taken as the proband, so II-2 = mother and II-4 = maternal aunt (sister of II-2 on the pedigree). Ages at death of proband, mother and father were calculated from birth/death years in the pedigree (2018-1966, 2018-1944, 2016-1942) and are approximate. 'RH+' (hormone receptors) recorded as ER pos and PR pos, and 'RH-' as ER neg and PR neg (aunt's tumour called triple negative in the text). Breast histology not given (nos). Mother's ovarian histology not given (nos). Maternal grandmother had cancer of unknown site at 56, so she is left out (no site code). The proband's II-2/II-4 cancers were found before the variant was detected; variant first missed by Sanger and early NGS.

cases.variant: c.829_832delAATA p.(Asn277Leufs*20) (NM_007294.3), frameshift; authors classify it as pathogenic under ACMG (PVS1, PM2, PP3), described as 'probably pathogenic' in the results
cases.citation: Ostrowska M et al. J Genomics 2022;10:33-38
cases.evidence: 'Here, we present a case report of serous ovarian cancer in a 67-year-old female patient.' 'The patient, a 67-year-old female, underwent right-sided mastectomy for breast cancer (NST, G2, T2N0M0) in 2011 ... ascites and tumors of the left and right adnexa were detected in September [2017] ... Diagnosis: G2 ovarian serous cancer with metastases to the abdomen.' 'Blood samples were collected from the proband's daughter, who had breast cancer in 2017, and from the proband's healthy son.' 'The proband was referred to genetic counseling since her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer (Figure 1).' 'A new variant was detected in the proband and the proband's daughter. This change was not detected in the son's samples.' Fig 1: '(I) mother with breast cancer, (II) proband with breast and ovarian cancer, and (III) daughter with breast cancer'; mother drawn as deceased.
cases.notes: The proband is described as 67 years old; it is not stated whether that is her age at the 2017 ovarian diagnosis or at the time of the report, so ovarian age 67 is approximate and the 2011 breast cancer age is left blank (about 61 if she was 67 in 2017). 'NST' breast cancer = invasive carcinoma of no special type, which maps to idc, but kept as nos because 'NST' could be read either way - judgement call (idc would also be reasonable). Ovarian 'G2 serous' entered as high-grade serous (in the two-tier system grade 2-3 serous carcinoma is high-grade); ovgrade left blank because the paper does not say high-grade. Daughter's age at diagnosis not given. The variant was first found by NGS in tumour tissue and then confirmed germline by Sanger in blood (proband and daughter).

cases.variant: c.2808_2811delACAA p.(Ala938Profs*21), frameshift
cases.citation: Huszno J et al. Prz Menopauzalny 2019;18:227-229
cases.evidence: 'A 75-year-old patient was admitted to the Genetic Outpatient Clinic ... with a diagnosis of right breast cancer and with a family history of cancer (two daughters who were diagnosed with breast cancer at ages 46 and 38 years).' 'Histopathological examination revealed ductal invasive carcinoma ... NST NG-3 G-3, Ki-67 75%, ER (+++), PR (+++), and without upregulated HER2 expression.' 'The c.2808_2811delACAA p. (Ala938Profs) mutation was observed in the BRCA2 gene.' 'One daughter was diagnosed aged 41 in 2010 ... ductal invasive carcinoma, pT2pN2, ER (++), PR (+++) and HER2 that was not upregulated.' 'The second daughter was diagnosed aged 38 years in 2014 ... lobular invasive carcinoma G2, ER (+), PR (+), HER2 that was not upregulated ... numerous metastases in the CNS ... the presence of the c.2808_2811delACAA ... mutation in the BRCA2 gene was confirmed ...; the same mutation was reported in her father.'
cases.notes: Age of the first daughter is inconsistent: 46 in the introduction and case summary, 41 in the detailed history ('diagnosed aged 41 in 2010'); 41 was used as it is the more specific statement. Proband's age 75 is his age at referral with the breast cancer diagnosis (treated 2018). Only the second daughter is stated to carry the variant; the first daughter tested negative for Polish founder mutations, her BRCA2 c.2808_2811del status is not stated. No other relatives are described.

cases.variant: W1692fs*3 (p.Trp1692fs), found on tumour NGS (FoundationOne CDx) and confirmed germline
cases.citation: Mauri G et al. World J Surg Oncol 2023;21:118
cases.evidence: Fig 1D legend: 'Pedigree of the proband diagnosed with a germline BRCA2 W1692fs*3 mutation following its identification by somatic tumor next generation sequencing (NGS) ... Her sister, who tested negative ... is indicated by a (-) symbol. Instead, her female cousin resulted positive ... The number represents the age of BRCA2 testing or cancer diagnosis, whichever comes first, and the organ represents the site of cancer origin (AC, ampullary cancer; OC, ovarian cancer; ALL, acute lymphoblastic leukemia).' Pedigree: proband III 'AC, 42' (+); father's sister II 'OC, 71' (not tested); father's brother II 'ALL, 50' (deceased, not tested); paternal first cousin (daughter of the OC aunt) '+', '50', unaffected. Text: 'NGS analysis revealed pathogenic mutations of BRCA2 (W1692fs*3 with a variant allele frequency (VAF) of 44%)'; 'the BRCA2 W1692fs*3 was confirmed germline'; histology 'ampullary adenocarcinoma' with CDX2 immunostaining (Fig 2).
cases.notes: Ampullary adenocarcinoma has no specific site code; entered as small bowel/duodenum adenocarcinoma (ampulla of Vater, CDX2-positive, i.e. intestinal-type). Biliary tract would be the alternative choice - judgement call. Relationship of the OC and ALL relatives inferred from the pedigree (siblings of the proband's father, the cousin being the OC aunt's daughter); the numbers in the pedigree are 'age of BRCA2 testing or cancer diagnosis, whichever comes first', so 71 and 50 are taken as diagnosis ages. Ovarian histology not given (nos). Unaffected carrier cousin and non-carrier sister omitted. Proband's current age not stated (diagnosed 2019, alive Dec 2022). A somatic FANCA variant (3% VAF) is not germline and is not relevant. [18 Oct 2026, new form options: ampullary adenocarcinoma recoded as ampullary carcinoma (biliary tract / ampulla).]

cases.variant: c.757_758delCT (written c.757-758TAG>T), p.Leu253fs (NM_024675.3), frameshift
cases.citation: Fewings E et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2018;3:489-498
cases.evidence: 'A heterozygous 2 bp frameshift deletion was identified in PALB2 (c.757-758TAG->T [rs180177092, NM_024675.3]) in a patient from family 4 who was diagnosed with diffuse gastric cancer at age 55 years (figure 2) ... Family 4 has a history of breast, lung, laryngeal, and diffuse gastric cancer (table 1, figure 2). Exome sequencing was also done on two unaffected siblings, one of whom also had the PALB2 ... variant.' Table 1 family 4: proband age 55; relatives 'Breast cancer, lung cancer, laryngeal cancer, gastric cancer, and diffuse gastric cancer (44, 52)'; candidate gene PALB2. Fig 2A pedigree: individual 2 (male) 'Diffuse gastric cancer (55) PALB2+/-'; brothers 'Diffuse gastric cancer (44)' (deceased) and 'Diffuse gastric cancer (53)'; mother 'Breast cancer' (deceased); father deceased, unaffected; father's siblings: 'Laryngeal cancer' (deceased), 'Lung cancer' (deceased), 'Gastric cancer'; father's mother 'Breast cancer' (deceased). Families from the UK Familial Gastric Cancer study (MREC 97/5/32), CDH1-negative.
cases.notes: Proband = individual 2 in Fig 2A (the sequenced affected case). Brother's age is 53 in the pedigree but 52 in Table 1; pedigree value used. The gastric-cancer relative of the father's generation is drawn as a male sibling of the father (paternal uncle); his age and histology are not given (nos), and from the drawing it is not clear whether he is deceased. Laryngeal cancer coded as head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: histology is not stated, but SCC is the only head and neck code - judgement call. Paternal grandmother's and mother's breast cancer ages not given. Unaffected carrier sibling (individual 1, male) and non-carrier sister omitted; another sibling drawn as deceased without cancer omitted. Variant written in the paper's VCF-like notation; c.757_758delCT is the HGVS form of the same 2 bp deletion (Leu253fs). Country: families recruited through the UK Familial Gastric Cancer study, Cambridge. [18 Oct 2026, new form options: laryngeal cancer of unstated histology recoded "type not known".]

cases.variant: c.892delGinsTTT p.(Glu298Phefs*48) (NM_000546.6), frameshift; likely pathogenic per authors
cases.citation: Papadimitriou DT et al. Children (Basel) 2023;10:1150
cases.evidence: 'A 15-month-old girl (generation V, Figure 1) consulted because of a marked change in clitoris size and pubarche ... Adrenal ultrasound detected a large tumor 5 cm in diameter at the left side ... Histology confirmed adrenocortical carcinoma.' 'family history (Figure 1): (a) of a maternal cousin aged 15 years who was operated on for an adrenocortical tumor at the age of 5 months and (b) of the maternal grandmother diagnosed of bilateral breast cancer at the age of 35 years ... other members of the maternal family were diagnosed with osteosarcoma (generation III), tumors of the cervical spine (generation I, II, and III), pancreas (generation III), uterus (generation II), and stomach and colon (generation III), the latter dying at the age of 25 years ... three members of the paternal family of our patient's mother had a history of two highly malignant neoplasms cases: a male subject aged 20 years deceased from lung cancer (generation II) and a female with sarcoma deceased at 24 years (generation III), but no clear transmission pattern to our patient's mother.' Variant found in patient, mother and maternal grandmother. Mother aged 26: 'unilateral in situ grade III ductal carcinoma of the right breast ... HER2+ ... estrogen receptor 30% weak positive, progesterone receptor <10% positivity'; 'Five years later, gynecological follow-up showed indices of cervical malignancy'. 'Seven years after the initial diagnosis, a lesion in the tibia ... A biopsy revealed osteosarcoma.' Pedigree: grandmother 'Bilateral breast cancer at 35, now 47, #7'; her brother 'Died at 35 from pancreatic cancer', his daughter '15 years ... Operated successfully at 5 months from adrenal cancer'; her sisters 'Died from osteosarcoma' and 'Died at 25 from CA of the stomach and colon'; her mother 'Died at 40 from CA of the uterus'; grandfather's brother 'Died from lung cancer at 20'; grandfather's niece 'Died from sarcoma at 24'.
cases.notes: Relationships taken from the pedigree. The adrenocortical-tumour 'maternal cousin' in the text is drawn as the daughter of the maternal grandmother's brother, i.e. the mother's first cousin (first cousin once removed of the proband) - no code, entered as m_other; her tumour is 'adrenocortical tumor'/'adrenal cancer' operated at 5 months, entered as ACC at age 0. The lung cancer (grandfather's brother) and sarcoma (grandfather's brother's daughter, entered as m_other) relatives are on the mother's paternal side, which the authors say shows no clear transmission; included because they are part of the reported maternal family history. Sarcoma type not given, entered as other soft tissue sarcoma (no 'unknown' option) - judgement call. Osteosarcoma age in the proband is approximate: 'seven years after the initial diagnosis' at 15 months (about 8). Mother's DCIS: ER '30% weak positive' and PR '<10% positivity' entered as pos (PR could be read as negative/low) - judgement call; she later had a local invasive recurrence. Mother's cervical malignancy age not given (about 31). 'Tumors of the cervical spine' in a great-great-grandfather, his son and grandson (generations I-III, deaths at 65, 65 and 15) were left out: no site code and nature of the tumours unknown. Mother's current age not stated. [18 Oct 2026, new form options: sarcoma of unstated type recoded "type not known".]

cases.variant: c.1101-1G>A (intron 10 acceptor splice site), ClinVar SCV001161439; authors argue for pathogenic, previously reported as VUS and as likely pathogenic
cases.citation: Prejac J et al. World J Surg Oncol 2021;19:254
cases.evidence: 'A 36-year-old woman presented with mastalgia and yellowish discharge from her right breast. She reported family history (maternal lineage) positive for cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with BC at 33 and died, and maternal grandmother at 65 years, also from BC. Uncle who had been a smoker died of lung cancer at the age of 70.' '... showed solitary mediastinal mass which was surgically removed. Patohistological examination revealed fibrous tumor with increased mitotic activity, positive for CD34 and STAT6.' 'after 4 years of follow-up, a lesion in the upper left quadrant of the right breast was discovered ... luminal B-like invasive BC ... pT1bN1 grade 3 carcinoma (ER 100%, PR 80%, Her2 negative ...).' Later pulmonary metastases 'consistent with metastasis of malignant fibrous tumor'. 'confirmed a germline single nucleotide variant: (c.1101-1G>A) in TP53 gene ... consistent with LFS.' 'Our particular case and its clinical manifestation provide additional arguments for this variant to be considered pathogenic.'
cases.notes: Malignant solitary fibrous tumour coded as other soft tissue sarcoma (the authors call SFT a type of sarcoma). Breast cancer age taken as 40 (found 'after 4 years of follow-up' from presentation at 36) - approximate; histology not stated (nos). Uncle assumed maternal (family history described as maternal lineage); the uncle's age 70 is his age at death from lung cancer, used also as diagnosis age. The grandmother's 65 is given as her age at breast cancer diagnosis (she also died of it). Variant classification: authors say it is 'consistent with LFS' and argue it should be pathogenic; prior ClinVar entries were VUS and likely pathogenic. No other living relatives; 3-year-old son untested.

cases.variant: Duplication of exons 6-13 (~23 kb, intron 5 to intron 13 breakpoints; NM_007194.3), predicted frameshift at codon 488 with premature stop at codon 503
cases.citation: Tedaldi G et al. BMC Cancer 2014;14:478
cases.evidence: 'The first family member who came to our attention ... was a woman aged 36 (III-4) who did not have cancer but had a high family incidence of breast cancer (Figure 1). Her mother (II-3) had bilateral breast cancer at 46 years old and 56 years old; three aunts had breast cancer at 70 years old (II-5), 50 years old (II-9) and 40 years old (II-11); and another aunt died of ovarian cancer at 40 years old (II-1). The grandfather of the proband (I-1) died of prostate cancer at 80 years old. Furthermore, the brother of the proband (III-5) has a clinical suspicion of neurofibromatosis ... and a cousin's daughter (IV-1) developed leukaemia at 3 years old.' 'The mother of the proband (II-3) and her aunt (II-5), both of whom had had breast cancer, had the same duplication in CHEK2.' 'the duplication ... created a frameshift at codon 488 ... resulting in a premature termination at codon 503.' Fig 1: II-1 (grey, deceased), II-3 (black, +/-), II-5 (black, +/-), II-7 (unaffected, -/-), II-9 (black, deceased), II-11 (black, deceased), I-1 (grey, deceased), IV-1 (grey) is the daughter of III-7, child of II-5.
cases.notes: The proband (III-4) is an unaffected carrier, as reported; the paper calls her mother the 'index case' for earlier BRCA testing. Aunts are maternal (siblings of II-3 in the pedigree), and the grandfather is the mother's father. Prostate cancer histology not stated; entered as adenocarcinoma - judgement call (nos not available for prostate). Leukaemia type not given, entered as haematological 'other'. Brother III-5 (carrier) has 'multiple subcutaneous cysts similar to neurofibromas' and suspected neurofibromatosis under investigation - left out as unconfirmed. Breast histology not given. The authors present the duplication as deleterious (frameshift) but say further studies are needed; it appears to be the same exon 6-13 duplication as in chek2-eu1 (Germani 2022) but in a separate family from a different centre (Meldola vs Rome). [18 Oct 2026, new form options: prostate cancer and leukaemia of unstated type recoded "type not known".] [18 Oct 2026, new form options: ]

cases.citation: Guadagnolo D et al. Biomedicines 2023;11:2062
cases.evidence: 'The proband (II:3) was a 65-year-old man referred for clinical genetics evaluation for a personal and familial history of gastric cancer. He was diagnosed with stage II intestinal type gastric cancer at 45 years of age ... He reported a sister (II:2) deceased due to diffuse gastric cancer at age 30, with an unaffected 44-year-old daughter (III:1). He also reported a 70-year-old sister (II:6) who had developed gastric diffuse cancer at age 52 and ovarian serous cancer at age 54. The parents of the proband died from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the father (I:1) at age 77 and the mother (I:2) at age 71.' 'Molecular testing identified the heterozygous c.5944C>T, p.(Gln1982*) variant in the ATM gene ... in the proband (II:3), his sister (II:6), and his niece (III:1), indirectly confirming the carrier status of the deceased individual (II:2).' 'It can be classified as "Pathogenic" according to the ACMG guidelines.'
cases.notes: Sister II:2's age at death taken as 30 ('deceased due to diffuse gastric cancer at age 30'), used for both diagnosis and death. Ovarian cancer is 'serous' with grade not stated, so entered as nos (could be high- or low-grade serous). Unaffected carrier niece and parents without cancer omitted.

cases.variant: Deletion of exons 5-9 (36,637 bp, Alu-mediated, breakpoint in intron 4); reduced exon 7-9 transcripts
cases.citation: Schnurbein G et al. Breast Cancer Res 2013;15:R120
cases.evidence: 'We identified a large heterozygous RAD51C deletion encompassing exons 5 to 9 in two independent families (Figure 1A,B,C). In the first (family #1), remarkably a BC-only family (Figure 1A), the mutation carrier was affected by early-onset and bilateral BC (age 33 years, age 39 years). The deletion was inherited from the mother who was affected by colon cancer (age 44 years).' 'all three RAD51C-positive breast tumors were classified as intermediate to high grade (individual #1-IV-2: G3, G3 ...), invasive ductal, and triple negative.' Fig 1A family #1: IV-2 'BC (33&39) Δexon 5-9'; mother III-6 'CC (44)' (deceased); maternal grandmother II-2 'BCL (78)' (deceased); maternal grandfather II-3 'RCC (65)'; II-1 (sister of II-2, child of I-1/I-2) 'BC (55)' (deceased); father III-7 and brother IV-1 'neg'. Legend: 'BCL, B-cell lymphoma; RCC, renal cell carcinoma; CC, colon cancer'.
cases.notes: Family #1 of two families in the paper was used (family #2: twins with BC 42 and OC 43, brother NHL 19), taken in order of description. Both breast cancers recorded as one bilateral entry (age 33, second side 39), both G3 IDC triple negative. Mother is an obligate carrier (deceased, father and brother tested negative). II-1 is the sister of the maternal grandmother (maternal great-aunt). Renal cell carcinoma subtype not stated (kidney nos). B-cell lymphoma coded as lymphoma.

cases.variant: VHL c.340C>T (heterozygous; called pathogenic by the authors; probable de novo in proband)
cases.citation: Cordeanu EM et al. JACC Case Rep 2025;30(41):105849
cases.evidence: 'A 57-year-old woman was admitted ... An abdominal computed tomography scan disclosed a 6 x 6 x 6 cm left adrenal mass highly suggestive of pheochromocytoma'; histology: 'characteristic pheochromocytoma features'. 'Postoperatively, comprehensive genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the VHL gene (c.340C>T)'. 'Her 2 sons underwent genetic testing: the elder son (age 26 years) tested positive for the same VHL mutation and subsequently underwent adrenalectomy for left adrenal pheochromocytoma, while the younger son (age 25 years) tested negative'. 'The patient's complex medical history further included invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast diagnosed 6 months postadrenalectomy'. 'She also developed a toxic thyroid adenoma'. Pedigree (Fig 2): 'The proband (II-2, age 57) ... Given the absence of VHL-related disease in previous generations, this likely represents a de novo mutation ... elder son (III-1, age 26), who underwent prophylactic adrenalectomy in 2024'.
cases.notes: Phaeo age 57 = age at admission. Breast IDC was diagnosed 6 months after adrenalectomy; exact age not stated, so left blank (about 57-58). The ages in the pedigree (57, 26) are taken as current ages; son's phaeo age entered as 26 (age given in text when he tested positive and had adrenalectomy) - approximate. The son's adrenalectomy is called 'prophylactic' in the legend but the text says it was 'for left adrenal pheochromocytoma'; coded as phaeo. Toxic thyroid adenoma (benign, not multinodular goitre) and stage 3a CKD not coded. Younger son tested negative and is omitted. Previous generations unaffected (probable de novo).

cases.variant: SDHB exon 6 c.587-591delC frameshift (as written by the authors; 'new germinal frameshift mutation')
cases.citation: da Silva ME et al. Hered Cancer Clin Pract 2012;10(1):12
cases.evidence: 'The authors present the clinical course of a 47 years-old female patient with a familial paraganglioma'. '37 years-old caucasian female, without known diseases until 1997 ... Abdominal CT showed a 5.2 cm mass in the region of the left adrenal gland ... Intraoperatively it was found that the lesion was separated from the adrenal gland ... made the diagnosis of malignant paraganglioma. Genetic screening of the patient demonstrated a new germinal frameshift mutation of the SDHB exon 6 [c.587-591DelC]. There was a family history of a cousin diagnosed at 13 years of age with a dopamine producing malignant paraganglioma, that died at 30 years of age with wide spread metastasis [cranial and lumbar].' Later local recurrence and T11 vertebral metastasis. 'The patient's direct family was offered genetic screening, having been diagnosed 5 positive patients, and one already died of metastatic pheocromocytoma'.
cases.notes: Proband's tumour was extra-adrenal, next to the left adrenal: coded ppgl/ta at 37 (1997); recurrence/metastases not entered as new primaries. The cousin's side of the family and sex are not given, so coded 'other'; the abdominal/thoracic location of the cousin's paraganglioma is not stated (cranial and lumbar were metastases) - coded ppgl/ta as the most likely for a dopamine-secreting malignant SDHB PGL, but this is a judgement. The relative who 'died of metastatic pheocromocytoma' is probably the same cousin, so not entered twice. The paper does not give the cousin's sex; entered as M only because the format requires a sex (arbitrary).

cases.variant: SDHAF2 c.232G>A, p.(Gly78Arg) (Dutch founder variant; called pathogenic by the authors)
cases.citation: de Jong MAM et al. Case Rep Otolaryngol 2024;2024:2111531
cases.evidence: 'The patient had presented at the age of 14 years with two slowly progressing swellings on both sides of the neck, diagnosed as bilateral carotid body tumors'. 'The family history revealed a father, aunt, and grandfather in the paternal lineage with multiple head and neck paragangliomas (Table 2). Some of the affected family members had been identified as carriers of the pathogenic c.232G > A, p.Gly78Arg variant in SDHAF2'. 'at the age of 27 ... the MRI showed bilateral vagal paragangliomas'. 'At the age of 34, the patient was diagnosed with an additional jugulotympanic paraganglioma on the left side'. 'At the age of 49 ... A new solid lesion of 3 cm at the head of the pancreas ... Cytology of the head of the pancreas also showed paraganglioma ... multiple paravertebral spinal bone lesions ... localization of paraganglioma within the spinal bone ... Both specimens showed negative SDHB immunohistochemistry'. 'No other primary sympathetic paragangliomas or pheochromocytomas were found in the abdomen or thorax.' Table 1 lists bilateral carotid (14), bilateral vagal (27), jugulotympanic (34), pancreas head (49), paravertebral and lung metastases (49). Table 2 is a pedigree image (affected individuals shaded).
cases.notes: Proband is a 49-year-old man at presentation of metastases with 27 months follow-up and catecholamines to age 52; ageNow 52 is approximate. Bilateral carotid body tumours entered once at 14 and bilateral vagal PGLs once at 27 (ppgl has no side field). The pancreatic-head paraganglioma is entered as a separate thoraco-abdominal (sympathetic) primary because the authors list it apart from the metastases and write 'No other primary sympathetic paragangliomas' - it could instead be a metastasis. Bone and lung metastases not entered. Relatives' ages not given; aunt and grandfather placed on the paternal side as the text states ('in the paternal lineage'). Paternal transmission pattern is typical of SDHAF2.

cases.variant: RET exon 16 c.2753T>C, p.Met918Thr (M918T; de novo - absent in father, mother and sister)
cases.citation: Paragliola RM et al. BMC Endocr Disord 2015;15:30
cases.evidence: 'In March 2010 a 24 year old Caucasian man with marphanoid habitus ... Four years earlier he had undergone total thyroidectomy with lymphadenectomy due to MTC (pT4N+; stage III UICC 2009) ... his family history was negative for MEN2B-related tumors.' 'mucosal neuromas of the tongue were found'. 'The genetic test for RET germline mutations showed the substitution of methionine for threonine in exon 16 at codon 918 (p.M918T) which was not present in other family members (father, mother and sister).' 'Histology of the adrenal glands confirmed the presence of bilateral and multifocal adrenal PHEO.' 'The histology of the right kidney mass revealed a capsulated neoplasm ... suggestive for reninoma.' 'Currently, 3 years after surgery, the patient is tumor-free.'
cases.notes: Single proband with a strongly characteristic MEN2B presentation (de novo M918T; no family history). MTC age 20 = 'four years earlier' than age 24. ageNow 27 = 24 + 3 years follow-up (approximate). The juxtaglomerular reninoma (benign renal tumour) is entered as kidney/nos because it is a renal tumour with no specific code; it is not a renal cell carcinoma and could be left out. Mucosal neuromas and marfanoid habitus have no code. The coding variant c. notation is not in the paper (only p.M918T); c.2753T>C is the standard notation for M918T.

cases.variant: MEN1 exon 4 c.781C>T, p.(Leu261Phe) (called a pathogenic variant by the authors; ClinVar single submission VUS; UMD-MEN1 'causal')
cases.citation: Gilis-Januszewska A et al. Genes (Basel) 2021;12(4):512
cases.evidence: 'A large Polish family was identified in which three generations had a MEN1 variant ... Genetic screening revealed a MEN1 pathogenic variant in other five family members, four of whom had clinical symptoms.' Index II.3, 'born in 1953 ... first admitted in 1996 ... An insulin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor was confirmed by histopathology'; 'The diagnosis of primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) was confirmed in 2007 ... Parathyroid adenoma was identified via histopathology'; 2018 'A non-functional tumor (18 x 10 mm) was detected in the left adrenal gland'; 'cutaneous collagenomas'. Brother II.4 'born in 1955 ... hypercalcemia (2.7 mmol/L) and elevated PTH ... The right lobe and the isthmus as well as the parathyroid gland were resected in 2016. Histopathological examination revealed parathyroid adenoma'; 'An abdominal CT from 2016 revealed a 25-mm tumor of the uncinate process of the pancreas. Subsequent SRI confirmed an abnormal accumulation'. III.3 'A daughter of the index patient's brother was born in 1979 ... diagnosed with primary hyperparathyroidism. A subtotal parathyroidectomy was performed in 2014 ... In 2019, CT showed a 5-mm hypodense focal lesion in the corpus of the pancreas ... multiple cutaneous angiofibromas on the face'. III.5 'A son of the index patient's brother, born in 1980 ... Hypercalcemia in the course of primary hyperparathyroidism was confirmed ... parathyroidectomy with resection of the upper right, lower right, and lower left parathyroid glands in April 2015 ... parathyroid nodular hyperplasia. In 2014, bilateral adrenal tumors ... adenoma ... In 2015, MRI revealed a pituitary microadenoma ... 2016 ... 8-mm tumor ... corpus of the pancreas ... probable neuroendocrine tumor (synaptophysin+, chromogranin+)'. III.9 'born in 1991, was diagnosed at the age of 23 ... primary hyperparathyroidism ... total resection of three parathyroid glands in 2015 ... 2020 ... two pancreatic lesions ... neuroendocrine tumor'. Table 1: II.3 F 54; II.4 M 60; III.3 F 35; III.5 M 34; III.9 F 23.
cases.notes: Ages calculated from birth years and event years (e.g. index born 1953, insulinoma 1996 = 43; PHPT 2007 = 54, matching Table 1). Brother's PHPT dated to his first admission in 2015 (age 60, matches Table 1); pancreatic tumour 2016 (61) shown on imaging and SRI only. III.3's pancreatic lesions (2019, age 40) are imaging findings only; Table 1 records 'Pancreatic Tumor: Yes'. III.3's facial angiofibromas coded feature/tsc_skin, the only code for facial angiofibromas (a known MEN1 skin sign). III.5 had 3-gland nodular hyperplasia, coded parathyroid adenoma side 'multi'; III.9 had 3 glands removed, no histology given, so no side. ageNow values = 2021 (publication) minus birth year, approximate.
